newsitem.title: UK: Tanker chartering thin, old/new spread widening.
newsitem.headline: Tanker chartering thin, old/new spread widening.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering continued thin on Monday but despite the slower pace of fixing, rates held mostly steady although discounted rates for older vessels continued to attract many charterers, brokers said.
In the Mediterranean and West Africa brokers reported a shortage of modern tonnage but they saw enough older tonnage around to meet the current cross Mediterranean demand.
"Cepsa took older vessels quite happily last week -- not too good a sign for the modern tonnage owners," one broker said.
Cross Med freight assessments were little changed but in some cases older Suezmax tonnage was up to 10 points cheaper.
This gap is seen widening with avails of modern tonnage becoming thinner and owners of older ships expected to accept cheaper rates in order to get their vessels fixed.
In the Mideast Gulf/Red Sea region Asian charterers continued to dominate with few tankers seen fixed westwards.

Shipping brokers said rates out of the Middle East Gulf on VLCCs to Japan were slightly firmer at around W62.5, with South Korea and Singapore pegged slightly weaker at around W55 after trade for 240 at $49.50 to Taiwan last week. U.S. Gulf rates were holding steady around W52.5 despite the lack of chartering to the West.
In the U.K/continent aframaxes (80,000 tonners) continued to find employment with rates stuck at around W105.

West African chartering continued healthy for owners with Koch taking a further million barrels transatlantic at W87.5, compared with W82.5-85 last week, in addition to a VLCC to the U.S. Gulf at W62.5 last week.
The Caribbean market was holding steady at the lower levels with 70,000 tonners accepting W130. -- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
